lane: native-resolution lidar scarp channels (executed at the 100 m cell scale - IR-67-DATA-01)
hypothesis: LIDAR-01: a field built from the mirrored 1 m-derived scarp channels (amplitude/sharpness, scale persistence, tensor orientation coherence, dominant strike) plus the owner-reported habitat direction places unit-mass dots on the faults the organizers added and that the public databases compensate for, so the dots earn kernel credit while avoiding false-positive mass on already-mapped faults.
mechanism: z_combined = 0.55 * clip(lane_z, +-3) + 0.45 * clip(habitat_z, +-3) * novelty, with novelty 0 at 2 px from a mapped fault rising to 1 at 15 px; lane_z is the rank-normalised scarp-lane aggregate (scarp_pixel_fraction, step_fraction, tensor_coherence, orientation_coherence, snr_weighted_amplitude, relief_mean, scale_persistence, strike_concordance, dominant_strike); habitat = 0.40*rank(deq_n100a15) + 0.30*rank(rad_K) - 0.30*rank(ext_UK) + 0.15*vent_prox; field = exp(0.60 * clip(z, +-2.5)); a density-equalising CDF systematic sample with 3 px minimum separation emits the budget exactly.
named_non_fault_mimic: Fluvial terrace risers, channel cut banks, pluvial shoreline terraces, dirt roads/canals/field edges (the cultural mask is ABSENT - IR-67-MASK-01), landslide head scarps, and radiometric playa/agricultural potassium anomalies.
